Compiled ARM tests · no hardware audio claim
September 22 and 23, 2026

text.name: Description
text.text: How we separated reusable audio code from the board, and checked its behavior before connecting it to hardware.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: An original application needs more than a successful boot. It needs small components whose inputs, outputs and failure behavior are understood. We started an unpublished development kit with audio packing and extraction code that can build without a Roland image or an attached SP.

text.name: Stage explanation
text.text: A clean source copy reproduces the library and CPU test image with the same installed tools.

text.name: Stage scope
text.text: Schematic test sequence, not a recording of the SP. Passing CPU cases establish the checked buffer behavior; they do not establish sound output. Illustrative timing; no device connection.

text.name: Timeline title
text.text: From a contract to an independent component

text.name: Heading
text.text: Give each layer a smaller job

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Our display and control experiments had already produced original code, but much of a firmware experiment concerns one particular build or board state. Reusing that whole experiment would carry its assumptions into the next one. We separated portable processing from the code that knows how to reach the SP's peripherals or cooperate with Roland's application.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: For an audio helper, that meant accepting ordinary buffers and explicit counts. The caller owns memory and decides when processing runs. The helper has no heap allocation, hardware register access or scheduler dependency. A stock-version adapter can use it later without putting stock function addresses into the portable component.

text.name: Heading
text.text: State exactly what a frame contains

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The transmit packer writes explicit little-endian bytes. Each recovered frame contains fourteen audio values clipped to signed 20-bit range, an unchanged 32-bit auxiliary value and a sign-extended 16-bit control field. Those are logical positions. We had not established the physical meaning of every channel or control value, so the API does not name them as known sockets.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The receive helper has a different contract: select a stereo pair from sixteen signed 16-bit positions, apply the documented pair ordering and write the result. Neither helper starts a stream. Packing an all-zero buffer also cannot promise safe silence when the meaning of its non-audio fields remains unresolved.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Check the calls that should fail

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: A correct ordinary frame is only part of the test. We checked zero, partial and full blocks, byte ordering, clipping boundaries and output guards. Invalid lengths, counts or pointers must return before writing output. Input pages were protected during CPU tests so an accidental in-place change could not pass unnoticed.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The retained transmit report contains 47 passing compiled ARM cases across 967 frames. Receive extraction passes 94 cases across 1,571 frames. Separate research comparisons execute the stock routines on synthetic inputs; the RX comparison matches 2,048 frames byte for byte. These comparisons check a bounded computation, with peripherals and the audio task outside the fixture.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: A rejected call should leave the destination unchanged. Test that property directly, including the bytes just outside the declared output area.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: A helper can appear independent while quietly importing a project script or reading a local firmware dump. We copied the declared SDK source and test files into an isolated directory, then built using the installed compiler and Python tools. The static library and CPU test image matched the original outputs byte for byte.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: That result applies to the recorded toolchain and source set. It is not a claim that every compiler produces identical binaries. The CPU image also uses an artificial emulator address; it is a test artifact, not a firmware update. Keeping those artifacts separate prevents a successful local build from looking like an installation package.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The same structure lets later work add independently tested controls, transport or DSP without claiming that the whole sampler is complete. A module's tests travel with its source. Board adapters then need their own evidence for ownership, timing and the physical route they use.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: At this milestone, the SDK's public API and source license were still being finalized. It was an unpublished development foundation. The safe exercise below recreates one buffer-contract check using invented signed 16-bit samples. It deliberately omits the SP's transmit layout, unknown control fields and any hardware connection.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Reject a short buffer without changing it

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Run this standalone Python 3 example. It clips invented samples, writes little-endian bytes and verifies an all-or-nothing capacity check. It writes no files and needs no firmware.

text.name: Command
text.text:
00 80 ff ff 01 00 ff 7f
unchanged after rejection: True

text.name: Checkpoint note
text.text: The short destination retains every sentinel byte because validation happens before assignment. This is a simplified contract exercise, not the SDK implementation or a test of the SP's audio hardware.

text.name: Evidence text
text.text:
Compiled ARM tests · no hardware audio claim. The reports below are retained project records; their underlying files are not published here. Read the curated evidence record.

CPU and buffer tests do not establish DMA operation, physical channel identity, sound output or device timing.

The retained source records are not presented as a released SDK or permission to distribute vendor firmware.

The exercise models a generic signed 16-bit contract and must not be used as an SP frame definition.

text.text: For an audio helper, that meant accepting ordinary buffers and explicit counts. The caller owns memory and decides when processing runs. text.name: Heading
text.text: State exactly what a frame contains

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The transmit packer writes explicit little-endian bytes. Each recovered frame contains fourteen audio values clipped to signed 20-bit range, an unchanged 32-bit auxiliary value and a sign-extended 16-bit control field. Those are logical positions. We had not established the physical meaning of every channel or control value, so the API does not name them as known sockets.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The receive helper has a different contract: select a stereo pair from sixteen signed 16-bit positions, apply the documented pair ordering and write the result. text.name: Heading
text.text: Check the calls that should fail

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: A correct ordinary frame is only part of the test. We checked zero, partial and full blocks, byte ordering, clipping boundaries and output guards. text.name: Paragraph

text.text: A rejected call should leave the destination unchanged. Test that property directly, including the bytes just outside the declared output area.

text.name: Stage explanation

text.name: Stage scope

text.name: Timeline title

text.name: Heading
text.text: Be precise about which loader changed

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: An original APP1 application can contain its own upload service or second-stage loader. It still starts through the retained reset-time resident. That distinction explains why a successful application boot, USB update or return from a RAM program does not establish that we can replace the earliest boot code safely.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Our project keeps the enclosure closed. We also preserve the resident, APP0 and boot settings while recovery is unresolved. Those constraints leave useful work available: source-built components, CPU tests and experiments confined to already understood application behavior. They do not turn an unknown recovery route into a verified one.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Gather evidence without replacing the loader

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Read-only application surveys added physical evidence alongside the offline work. R17 recorded the running unit's boot configuration; R26 captured reset settings twice with matching results and unchanged USB status. Those R26 readings described that boot, not the earlier failed resets. Between them, R25 read the mapped resident window twice. Both 524,288-byte captures matched each other and the earlier R5 capture byte for byte. That supported repeatability and an unchanged mapped window through the intervening application updates. It was not a raw-chip backup or a demonstrated resident restore.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Separate software requests in R19 and R21 tried to reach the chip's built-in downloader. Neither test observed its expected USB device. The owner reported a dark screen with lights on, and full power removal restored the installed application, confirmed by fresh USB status. The exact point reached remained unknown. Returning after a power cycle did not prove a route that could recover a damaged resident.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: R33 later established a narrower result: one guarded normal watchdog reset made USB disappear and return with fresh diagnostic state and the expected reset flags. The owner confirmed the post-reset title and responsive controls. No ROM request or boot-area write occurred in that test. A working normal reset gave later experiments a tested component without resolving independent recovery.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: P12B connects the original transport, update state machine, storage backend and corrected session provider in one compiled runtime. Its tests check the sequence from received data through validation and modeled readback. They also check failures and whether a bus reset preserves the transaction's state.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: One retained test processes a 65,540-byte synthetic image and checks 69,632 bytes of modeled sector readback. Its 306 actions receive 306 acknowledgments. These figures describe an integrated CPU fixture. Peripheral responses, memory accessibility and storage completion still come from models; no physical cold boot or interrupted-write recovery follows from that count.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Keep confirmed and candidate state separate

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The trial coordinator explores how a future loader might remember a candidate without losing the confirmed image. It keeps two records and updates the inactive record first. A final commit marks a complete record. A newer pending record still names the old confirmed image until the intended trial is confirmed through the trusted session.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The compiled P2 tests cover 768 interruptions before individual byte changes and 42 adapter failures. The storage fixture models one-to-zero programming, but real erase and programming failures need not stop neatly at a byte boundary. CRC checks detect accidental corruption; they do not authenticate records or guarantee exactly-once behavior under every later corruption pattern.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: In a trial model, ask separately which record is complete, which image is confirmed and whether the current session actually ran the candidate. A newer record answers only the first question.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Make an unresolved assumption stop execution

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: P18 composes more of the proposed resident path, but its normal entry deliberately stops before selecting a new stack, calling C or copying and clearing RAM. We have not established that the intended memory is free from work by other hardware masters at that point. A linker map allocates addresses to our program; it cannot prove that the machine has stopped using them elsewhere.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Separate conditional CPU cases exercise the later path under an explicit ownership assumption. Those tests are useful for finding defects behind the hold. Repeating them cannot establish the missing physical ownership contract, so their success does not remove the hold or make the image an installation candidate.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Define what a recovery result must prove

text.name: Paragraph

A software request issued by a working application cannot, on its own, satisfy independent entry.

It demonstrates why committing candidate metadata does not automatically make that candidate the confirmed image. It contains no device interface, storage addresses or installation procedure.

text.name: Article title
text.text: A synth that belongs on the SP

text.name: Description
text.text: Designing a live instrument around the pads, knobs and capture workflow, while testing how it could share Roland's sampler.

text.name: Period
text.text: September 29, 2026 · design and contract milestone / Research

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The owner chose live playing followed by resampling to a pad. That choice shaped the interface and the integration research: an original synth engine should work inside the existing sampler, with a clear path from playing a sound to keeping a take.

text.name: Stage explanation
text.text: CPU tests constrain the stock mixing contract. Device timing, memory ownership and a usable synth package still need evidence.

text.name: Stage scope
text.text: Schematic proposed workflow, not an implemented SP feature. The design and CPU tests do not establish live synthesis or capture on hardware. Illustrative timing; no device connection.

text.name: Timeline title
text.text: Follow the phrase from patch to pad

text.name: Heading
text.text: Design around playing, then keeping a phrase

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The request was for a subtractive synth inspired by Ableton Drift, with a broad set of sounds and an interface that fits the SP. The owner specified an addition to Roland's firmware and selected live playing followed by resampling. We used those choices to judge the design: playing and capturing should remain understandable without turning the small screen into a desktop synth panel.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Drift supplied an interaction and feature reference. The planned engine uses original DSP and patches; it does not claim to reproduce Drift's proprietary sound. A proposed 128-patch library is a content target. It says nothing about the number of simultaneous notes the SP can sustain alongside its sampler.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Trace where a generator joins the sampler

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The stock research found a generator mixer in transmit preparation. It adds generated samples to one selected stereo pair in a fourteen-position working buffer. That gives the adapter a specific computation to verify before considering an original source of samples. A receive buffer used by recording code would not establish the same output route.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: We executed the actual mixer in 294 CPU cases, checking enable state, frame count, pair selection, pan and the gain ramp. A deterministic stub supplied the samples. The tests establish the checked additions and unaffected positions; they do not execute a complete oscillator or establish an audible socket, available CPU time or safe memory reservation.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Keep the producer test narrower than the synth

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: A later fixture exercised thirty-six direct phase sweeps through selected stock waveforms. The saw, triangle and pulse results matched reference values within one integer count and established a signed 16-bit return value. Each phase was assigned directly, so the result does not measure pitch or a continuously advancing oscillator.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The broader attempt was excluded because its runtime and random-number setup was incomplete. Emulator CPU models also rejected instructions used by the fixture, requiring a model suited to the scalar arithmetic being checked. We retained those limits instead of describing the test as qualification of the SP processor. Noise, hardware clock rate and physical output remained outside it.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Review the screens after each action

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The Penpot concept grew to twenty-eight proposed screen states using editable display components and the shared SP panel. Early review found missing take recall, octave feedback and confirmations, along with inconsistent SHIFT wording. Those findings led to explicit routes for the actions a player could actually take.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The next review caught a subtler error: Initialize and Store still led to a screen showing the old edited patch. Corrected success states update the patch name and edited marker while preserving the intended take state. An enlarged saved-patch export then clipped a label's final character. A subsequent native recapture showed MOTION and SPACE in full, and the focused R2 review passed with the saved patch and retained take still correct. That review cleared the affected design fixes, not the whole interface or its future firmware rendering.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: After a confirmation, inspect the destination screen. The patch name, edited marker and take status should describe the completed action, including what survived it.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Separate generated audio from a captured performance

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: The stock export trace disables live generation and renders samples synchronously into a PCM file. That behavior establishes generated-file export. It does not establish capture of the phrase just played, so the requested live-to-pad workflow still needs a verified recording route and a clear ownership and lifetime contract for the take.

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Original oscillators, envelopes and filters are being developed separately from that adapter. A staged source file or test definition is not a passing engine result. At this design-and-contract milestone, there was no installable synth package or physical audio result. Voice limits, listening tests and behavior under simultaneous sampler load remain measurements to make before presenting the concept as a finished instrument.

text.name: Heading
text.text: Make success screens follow the state

text.name: Paragraph
text.text: Run this fictional patch-state example in Python 3. It models cancel, initialize and store entirely in memory. Its names and behavior are an exercise, not the SP's current firmware interface.

text.name: Command
text.text:
cancel: Example patch / edited / phrase-1
initialize: Init / clean / phrase-1
store: My patch / clean / phrase-1

text.name: Checkpoint note
text.text: The labels come from the resulting state rather than copied screen text. The unchanged take is an explicit rule of this fictional example. Real firmware still needs defined storage failures, capture ownership and tested transitions.

text.text:

The interface is a proposed instrument workflow, not a claim of installed synth controls or physical audio.

CPU mixer and producer fixtures do not establish voice count, worst-case timing, live capture or stock sampler compatibility.

The research records identify retained local evidence; they are not public firmware downloads.
